title: Exploratory Analysis Report
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of exploratory analysis report and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply defining analytical questions in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Exploratory Analysis Report is part of Exploratory Data Analysis and Descriptive Statistics. Start with defining analytical questions and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Statistical conclusions depend on data quality, design, assumptions and uncertainty, not just the value returned by one function. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

items.title: Defining Analytical Questions
items.text: Explain defining analytical questions in the context of exploratory analysis report, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Producing Summary Tables
items.text: Explain producing summary tables in the context of exploratory analysis report, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

items.title: Creating a Visualization Set
items.text: Build the smallest example for creating a visualization set, inspect the returned object, and confirm its names, type and shape before using it downstream.

items.title: Recording Data Limitations
items.text: Compare recording data limitations using concrete trade-offs, assumptions and maintenance needs; state when each choice is appropriate.

items.title: Writing Evidence-Based Findings
items.text: Explain writing evidence-based findings in the context of exploratory analysis report, connect it to the example, and verify one expected result or edge case.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: State the question and assumptions, calculate a small example, and explain uncertainty or a limitation in context. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Exploratory Analysis Report
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 139: Exploratory Analysis Report
measurements <- c(8, 10, 12)
mean(measurements)
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Treat this as a descriptive calculation; state the sample/design assumptions before making an inferential claim. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For exploratory analysis report, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply exploratory analysis report to a small synthetic example. Start with defining analytical questions, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the defining analytical questions idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.
content.expected_output: A reproducible exploratory analysis report example or design sketch with the expected result, one checked edge or failure case, and a stated limitation.

Check labels, units, assumptions, diagnostics and uncertainty before interpreting the output.
Test a boundary, missing, invalid or failure input relevant to this topic.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
